core_obligations: Replace Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by an affine neighbourhood of x, then reduce to X integral by treating the irreducible components separately (proof lines 3605-3618).
Dispose of the case where the generic point of X maps to y, where X is a scheme over kappa(y) and the hypothesis applies directly (proof lines 3620-3622).

In the remaining case, factor X through Spec(B/q) for a minimal prime q distinct from the maximal ideal and apply the dimension formula; use dim(B/q) = 1 and the identity trdeg_{kappa(q)}(R(X)) = d from the hypothesis to bound dim(O_{X,x}) + trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) (proof lines 3623-3636).

Use that dim(O_{X,x}) > dim(O_{X_y,x}) since O_{X,x} is a Noetherian domain mapping onto the smaller ring with a kernel, obtain the upper bound dim_x(X_y) <= d, and combine it with the lower bound d coming from the openness of bounded fibre dimension (proof lines 3637-3649).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the local ring at y and to X integral (proof lines 3605-3618).
Split on the image of the generic point (proof lines 3620-3622).
Apply the dimension formula in the non-trivial case (proof lines 3623-3646).
Combine the upper bound with the lower bound from boundedness (proof lines 3647-3649).
difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type, a point x whose image has Noetherian local ring of dimension at most one, and an integer d such that every generic point of an irreducible component of X containing x has fibre dimension d, the lemma concludes dim_x(X_y) = d (statement lines 3596-3603). The proof replaces Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by an affine neighbourhood, reduces to X integral by handling the irreducible components separately, and then splits on whether the generic point of X maps to y (proof lines 3605-3622). In the remaining case the author factors X through Spec(B/q) for a minimal prime q distinct from the maximal ideal and applies the dimension formula: dim(O_{X,x}) + trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) <= dim(B/q) + trdeg_{kappa(q)} R(X), where dim(B/q) = 1 and the second transcendence degree equals d by the hypothesis, while dim(O_{X,x}) > dim(O_{X_y,x}) because the local ring is a Noetherian domain and the map has a kernel; the two inequalities squeeze dim_x(X_y) to d (proof lines 3623-3649). The claim is H2: the reductions are standard, while the dimension formula computation and the strict inequality between the local rings are the substantive steps.
